extracted.intended_audience: writers submitting to McSweeney's publications (Internet Tendency, Quarterly Concern, The Believer, McSweeney's Books)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writers about where and how to submit work to McSweeney's different outlets (Internet Tendency, Quarterly Concern, The Believer, and McSweeney's Books), including genre/format fit and publisher policies. Directs submitters to section-specific requirements and links to individual guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section selection / submit to appropriate section
rubrics_metrics.description: We have four different sections where you can submit your work. Some sections are open for subs more often than others, and editorial needs and submission requirements differ for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the correct McSweeney’s section for your work (Internet Tendency, Quarterly Concern, The Believer, or McSweeney’s Books) and follow that section's specific submission guidelines (links provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet Tendency: humor and satire
rubrics_metrics.description: “McSweeney’s Internet Tendency is our humor and satire site.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit material that fits humor/satire genres to the Internet Tendency; follow the Tendency’s specific submission page (linked) for formats, length, and editorial preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly Concern: print journal focused on short fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: “McSweeney’s Quarterly Concern is our print journal, which primarily features short fiction.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quarterly Concern primarily seeks short fiction for print—submit prose appropriate for a literary print journal and consult the Quarterly’s submission guidelines for length, formatting, and other requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Believer: literature, arts, and culture magazine
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Believer is our literature, arts, and culture magazine.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pieces on literature, arts, and culture belong with The Believer; check that magazine’s submission instructions for topical fit, style, and submission windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: McSweeney’s Books: book-length and varied genres
rubrics_metrics.description: “McSweeney’s Books is where we publish, you guessed it: books. From novels to story collections to nonfiction to poetry—and more.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For book-length projects (novels, story collections, nonfiction, poetry, etc.) submit to McSweeney’s Books following their book submission policies and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission availability varies (open windows differ)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Some sections are open for subs more often than others, and editorial needs and submission requirements differ for each.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect differing submission windows and editorial needs across sections; verify whether a section is currently accepting submissions before sending work.

rubrics_metrics.name: No AI-assisted writing; attestation required
rubrics_metrics.description: “McSweeney’s accepts no writing aided in any manner by AI. Before publishing any writing—from a letter to a book-length work—authors published at McSweeney’s will be asked to attest that AI played no part in the creation or writing of that work.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit work created or written with AI assistance. If published, you will need to formally attest that AI played no part in creating the work.
